hinglish.title: L-1.1: Introduction to Operating System and its Functions with English Subtitles
covers: goals/functions of an OS (process, memory, device, file management)
hinglish.why: By far the most-watched OS lecture in Hindi found (5.37M views, 119.6K likes, 3200 comments) and the natural entry point for the whole GATE OS unit, part of Gate Smashers' dedicated OS roadmap series. Comment sentiment is overwhelmingly positive ('legends watching before exam', many crediting it for passing semesters/interviews) with essentially no coverage or accuracy complaints found in the top 60 comments.
comment_highlights: Legends are watching it one day before the exam.
Blessed to have teacher like you....huge respect sir....

hinglish.title: L-1.7: System Calls in Operating system and its types in Hindi
covers: what a system call is and how it works
hinglish.why: Near 2M views with a strong like ratio (~1.5%) for a 10-minute lecture, and top comments confirm exact syllabus alignment: one highly-liked comment gives timestamps noting 'System calls shift from user mode to kernel mode' and points viewers to the companion user/kernel-mode video, showing the two topics are taught as a connected pair by this channel. No accuracy complaints surfaced in the top 60 comments, only gratitude for exam/interview prep.
comment_highlights: System calls shift from user mode to kernel mode.
Thank you for explaining in such easy way, the lecture was very interesting

hinglish.title: L-1.8: Fork System call with Example | Fork() system call questions
covers: counting number of processes created by n fork() calls (2^n fork-tree pattern)
hinglish.why: Directly targets the classic GATE PYQ pattern named in the syllabus: top comments independently reconstruct the exact 2^n fork-tree counting method taught in the video ('for 4 times a, it will be 2^4=16 times... 15 Child Processes, 1 Parent Process'), confirming both coverage and correctness. 1.32M views with an unusually high 1000 comments (highest engagement-per-view among the Hinglish finalists) and no complaints of errors found.
comment_highlights: Our education system needs more teachers like him!
Make Fork Tree and count total number of nodes at last level, for 4 times 2^4=16

english.title: Introduction to Operating Systems
covers: abstract view of a computer system (hardware/OS/programs/users)
english.why: The most-viewed English OS lecture found for this scope (4.15M views, 46.5K likes) from the most reputable English-medium GATE/CS channel (Neso Academy). Comments consistently praise clarity ('I love that you made us see why the OS is NECESSARY instead of just telling us what it does') with no accuracy complaints in the top 60.
comment_highlights: I love that you made us see why the os is NECESSARY instead of just telling us what it does.
For every CSE/EC/IT students, NESO academy is there for them!

english.title: System Calls
covers: what a system call is and how it works
user mode vs kernel mode / mode switching
english.why: Nearly 1M views with strong per-view engagement, and top comments confirm the video explicitly teaches user-mode/kernel-mode switching ('There are 2 modes of execution... User mode... Kernel mode', 'Switching from kernel to user and vice versa is known as mode shifting'), directly matching the syllabus item. International reach is notable ('easy to understand, many thanks from Ireland') with no error complaints seen; one viewer asked for a follow-up fork()/exec() video, which Neso separately provides.
comment_highlights: Switching from kernel to user and vice versa is known as mode shifting not context switch.
Very happy to find an explanation in English that is easy to understand. Many thanks from Ireland

english.title: fork() and exec() System Calls
covers: process creation (PID, parent/child output counting for simple examples)
english.why: Best available English, well-captioned, non-broad lecture specifically on fork()/exec(); comments call it 'The Best Explanation for fork() and exec() I ever saw' with praise from viewers worldwide (Greece, plus others unhappy with their own professors' 3-hour explanations). It does not, however, generalize to the full 2^n counting-for-n-fork()-calls GATE drill the way the Hinglish pick does (see coverage_gaps).
comment_highlights: The Best Explanation for fork() and exec() I ever saw. Hats off Sir!!
EXCELLENT EXPLANATION (hello from national technical university of Athens - Greece)

runners_up.reason_rejected: Well-regarded English fork() explainer (350K views, very positive international comments) but does not clearly teach the generalized 2^n counting-for-n-fork()-calls GATE pattern the way Neso's or Gate Smashers' picks do; Neso Academy's fork()/exec() video was preferred for higher views and channel reputation.

coverage_gaps: Neither language's 3-video pick set fully covers 'types of OS' (batch, multiprogramming, multitasking, time-sharing, real-time) since the best channels split this into separate videos and the 3-video cap forced prioritizing OS-definition + system-calls + fork()/counting instead. For Hinglish, supplement with Gate Smashers L-1.2 (povNcHSasgs), L-1.3 (3MqyDWDpZoI), L-1.4 (YQZbIT9FcUk) for types, and L-1.10 (8duV1LLHHJU) for a full dedicated user-mode-vs-kernel-mode treatment (the chosen L-1.7 only briefly touches mode-switching). For English, supplement with Sundeep Saradhi Kanthety's 'Types of Operating Systems' (s-tk8el8JoU) for types; user/kernel mode is reasonably covered inside the chosen Neso 'System Calls' video per verified comments. Additionally, the English fork() pick (Neso's fork()/exec()) teaches fork() semantics well but does not explicitly generalize to the 2^n process-counting formula for n fork() calls the way the Hinglish pick (Gate Smashers L-1.8) does -- students relying only on the English pick may need extra practice problems for that specific GATE pattern.
